mfg1-mechanical-weekly-08-q01.stem: Equal volumes of a specimen and reference water have specified masses of 72 g and 24 g. What is the ratio?
reasons: 72 minus 24 is 48, but the requested ratio uses division, not a difference.
24÷72 reverses the reference and specimen; it is not specimen divided by reference.
The equal-volume mass ratio is 72÷24=3. Distinguish it from a value carrying density units.
72+24=96 is total mass, not an equal-volume mass ratio.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-08-q02.stem: A protractor blade is lifted away while measuring a sloping face. What should you do first?
options: Check the two target faces and instrument contact.
Read only the number with the blade still lifted.
Change the angle into a unit of length.
Measure an easier-to-see face instead.
reasons: Without correct contact with both target faces, the requested angle has not been confirmed.
A reading with a lifted blade does not correctly represent the angle between the target faces.
Angle and length are different quantities; changing units cannot correct poor contact.
Another face changes the target rather than confirming the requested angle.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-08-q03.stem: You need hole depth, but measured only the top-face height from a surface plate. How should you handle it?
options: Use that height directly as depth.
Copy the drawing value as an actual measurement.
Mark depth checked whenever the contact moves.
Separately check the depth reference face and contact with the bottom.
reasons: Height from the plate and depth from a reference face to the bottom use different references and targets.
The drawing specifies a requirement; it must not be copied as an unmeasured depth result.
Contact movement alone does not establish bottom contact or the correct reference face.
Height and depth have different reference faces and targets.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-08-q04.stem: You noticed an unusual sound but only gave your supervisor a morning greeting. What further action is suitable?
options: Treat the nod as sufficient and omit reporting.
Clearly report the target, facts and action already taken.
Continue operation until the supervisor notices.
Ignore it because a safety officer is named.
reasons: A nod does not tell the other person which equipment has developed what condition.
A greeting builds a relationship; it does not replace a specific abnormality report.
Continuing without reporting an abnormality can spread danger.
Having a safety officer is not a reason to withhold discovered facts.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-08-q05.stem: You received operation training only for new equipment. May you also change internal settings alone?
options: Check the target and scope of training, qualifications and permission.
Do anything because it is the same equipment.
Treat reading the textbook as permission.
Set it using experience with the previous machine.
reasons: Operation training and permission for internal settings are not identical.
Even on one machine, operation and internal settings may require different training or authorization.
Reading a textbook does not replace workplace training, qualifications or work permission.
Previous-machine experience alone does not establish the present conditions or scope for internal settings.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-08-q06.stem: A cart load tilted, but nobody was injured. Which record is suitable?
options: Record nothing because there was no injury.
Report nothing until 300 events.
Record the place, action, surroundings and response as facts.
Blame carelessness without investigation.
reasons: An event without injury can still signal danger; no record means losing improvement information.
The ratio 300 is not a reporting-start criterion; report facts from each event.
Uninjured warning events contain improvement information; the ratio is not a condition for starting reports.
Blaming carelessness without facts overlooks equipment and environmental factors.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-08-q07.stem: A bolt will not enter easily. Someone proposes hammering the head before using an impact wrench. What should you do?
options: Hammer hard to make it fit.
Do not force it; check compatibility, foreign matter and damage by the procedure.
Accept crushed threads if it tightens.
Only turn tool output to maximum.
reasons: Hammering can damage threads and does not necessarily improve fit.
Impact damage to threads can cause poor fastening or injury.
Crushed threads impair engagement and fastening, and may later lead to detachment.
Ra ising output without checking mismatch or damage results in forced tightening.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-08-q08.stem: You place a density table beside a specific-gravity record. What should you check?
options: Treat similar numbers as identical values.
Always attach kg to specific gravity.
Directly use masses of different volumes as specific gravity.
Distinguish units, reference substance and temperature conditions.
reasons: Similar numbers can represent different quantities or units, so density and specific-gravity conditions need checking.
kg is a mass unit, not a unit to append to a dimensionless reference ratio.
A ratio of masses of different volumes is not the equal-volume comparison.
Specific gravity is a reference ratio, not density itself or an isolated mass.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-08-q09.stem: You want to pass a precision tolerance using only a steel-rule length reading. What should you do?
options: Any graduated tool can judge any tolerance.
Delete the unit and pass it.
Check suitability for the requirement and the specified instrument.
Enlarge the paper and measure it.
reasons: Graduations on a rule do not necessarily provide sufficient capability for the required tolerance.
Removing units neither improves capability nor supplies conformity evidence; it loses record information.
Instruments have purposes and reading capabilities; measure with the specified tool appropriate to the requirement.
Enlarging paper is not measuring the actual item or confirming instrument suitability.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-08-q10.stem: Chips are stuck to a height-gauge base. What is needed before measuring?
options: Add the foreign matter as part of the reference.
Zero the number only, with no cleaning.
Measure with the gauge still tilted.
Check the base and surface plate by the specified procedure.
reasons: Foreign matter changes contact with the plate and is not a valid part of the reference.
Changing the displayed zero alone does not remove instability from dirt on the base or plate.
Tilt does not give a height measured in the specified direction from the reference.
Height uses the plate as reference, so foreign matter under the base affects the value.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-08-q11.stem: Is it suitable to use Heinrich’s 1:29:300 as a definite forecast of next month’s workplace accidents?
options: No; distinguish it from an educational ratio encouraging attention to warning signs.
The counts must always be identical.
Wait for 300 events before addressing a serious accident.
Different counts prove there is no danger.
reasons: The ratio is not an inevitable prediction formula for every workplace.
It cannot be applied as a mandatory forecast of every workplace’s future incident counts.
Report warning signs when found, rather than waiting for a statistical count.
A count differing from the ratio does not negate a hazard or its seriousness.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-08-q12.stem: Walking under a suspended load would shorten the route. Which judgment is suitable?
options: Pass underneath if it is brief.
Follow access controls and use a safe route.
Hold the load by hand while passing.
Judge safety from rope color alone.
reasons: A short crossing does not remove falling-load danger or the need for access control.
Do not enter the danger zone to save distance when a load may fall.
Entering underneath to hold a load exposes you to falling or contact hazards.
Rope color alone does not establish the condition and suitability of the load, gear or lifting arrangement.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-09-q01.stem: Someone says you can enter an area with unknown gas because a dust mask is available. What should you do?
options: Particle capture means every gas is stopped too.
Stay out and check the substance and required protection and equipment conditions.
Decide performance from mask color.
Hold your breath and skip checks.
reasons: Particle filtration and gas protection are different; a particle filter does not establish protection against all gases.
Dust and gas need different protection, and oxygen deficiency needs a separate check.
Color or shape alone cannot establish protection for the substance.
Breath-holding does not replace equipment or protection required for gas or oxygen-deficiency hazards.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-09-q02.stem: Fire and smoke appear near wiring that may be energized. What is the priority?
options: Apply water and approach the supply.
Go alone deeper into the smoke to investigate.
Discharge an extinguisher without reading its marking.
Alert others from a safe location, securing an escape route and following emergency procedures.
reasons: Water at energized parts creates shock danger, and approaching the fire can cause secondary harm.
Reporting and safe evacuation take priority over investigating inside smoke.
An extinguisher requires suitability and safety checks; do not use it unconfirmed.
Prioritize reporting and evacuation, avoiding water on energized parts and dangerous approaches.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-09-q03.stem: After a special health examination, someone proposes stopping the cleaning-equipment hood. Is this suitable?
options: No; health checks and exposure-control equipment are different measures.
An examination prevents harmful substances being generated.
Good health means ventilation is unnecessary.
Protective equipment permits an unauthorized shutdown.
reasons: Health examinations do not replace source or airborne-exposure measures during work.
An examination does not remove substance generation or exposure during the task.
Present good health is not grounds to omit ventilation or source controls.
Protective equipment and engineering measures are separate; do not stop equipment without authorization.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-09-q04.stem: You have an unapproved idea to shorten a procedure. How should you proceed?
options: Rewrite only your own paper.
Try it before informing later processes.
Summarize the purpose and effects, and propose it through the formal change procedure.
Experience means approval is unnecessary.
reasons: Changing only your paper loses formal change control and consistency with other operators.
Unapproved action can affect other processes’ quality and safety.
Even an improvement can affect quality or safety, so the prescribed checks and approval are needed.
Length of experience is not grounds to omit change approval.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-09-q05.stem: An incorrect label is passed from manufacturing through shipping. What should a QC circle check?
options: Blame inspection alone.
Determine the cause by majority vote.
Ignore the shipping-side result.
Share departmental facts, handover identification and countermeasure effects.
reasons: A quality problem needs information from the whole flow; do not assume inspection alone caused it.
A vote chooses an opinion; it does not prove a cause from facts.
Ignoring the receiving shipping department leaves identification after action unverified.
Quality is supported across the flow; connect departmental information with effectiveness checks.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-09-q06.stem: You find an error in another person’s past inspection record. What should you do?
options: Ignore it because it is not your record.
Report it with the original record and target, and obtain correction and impact checks.
Delete the original data so it cannot be traced.
Treat every past value as correct.
reasons: Another person’s record can still affect products, so report a discovered error.
Traceable correction and impact-scope checks are needed regardless of who made the record.
Deleting source data prevents tracing the history and affected scope.
Past values are not automatically correct; confirm the error and its target.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-09-q07.stem: Only the voltage of relocated equipment is known; AC or DC is unclear. What should you do?
options: Equal voltage makes the type irrelevant.
Try a socket whose shape fits.
Withhold connection and check the nameplate and specified supply.
Assume DC is harmless.
reasons: Equal voltage with a different supply type or frequency may still be unsuitable.
Connector shape alone does not establish ratings; do not try energizing unknown equipment.
The supply type, frequency and ratings must match as well as the number.
DC is also hazardous; type alone cannot establish that shock is impossible.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-09-q08.stem: Only ordinary protective glasses were chosen for gas cutting. What additional check is needed?
options: Confirm specified light-filtering performance and task suitability.
Transparent glasses stop all light hazards.
Squinting replaces performance checks.
Decide only by glove thickness.
reasons: Protection from flying material and protection from cutting light require different checks.
Transparent impact glasses do not necessarily provide the required filtering for gas-cutting light.
Squinting does not replace specified eye protection.
Hand-protection thickness does not check the light hazard to the eyes.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-09-q09.stem: You have an extinguisher, but smoke has obscured the escape route. What should you do?
options: Always advance because you have an extinguisher.
Do not persist; follow evacuation and reporting procedures.
Stay in the smoke to find the suitability marking.
Run to the supply at the fire source.
reasons: Possessing an extinguisher does not restore a lost escape route; do not continue dangerously.
Initial firefighting requires a safe escape route and similar conditions, not dangerous approach.
Searching inside smoke delays evacuation and increases danger.
Running to the fire brings fire or shock exposure and is outside safe-position operation conditions.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-09-q10.stem: You are assigned to carry a heavy box. Which pre-start check is most suitable?
options: Check weight, shape, distance, route and specified assistance.
Practice until you can lift it alone.
Judge every hazard from one handling-posture point.
Take a shortcut under a suspended load.
reasons: Safe handling considers the method and surroundings as well as weight.
Do not force practice until you can lift alone; check weight and assistance first.
Posture alone does not check distance, route, shape and other hazards.
A shortcut under a suspended load has a falling-load hazard and is not a safe carrying route.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-09-q11.stem: Only you received the updated procedure; the next operator still has the old version. What is needed?
options: Your knowledge alone completes the update.
Either version may be chosen freely.
Mix old conditions from memory.
Check effective date, target, old-version separation and communication.
reasons: Changes must reach the people concerned; your own knowledge is insufficient.
Free choice between versions of unclear applicability disrupts consistency.
Mixing versions from memory may follow neither approved procedure.
The update must reach the next operator correctly and make the applicable version clear.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-09-q12.stem: An unjudged item is in a box scheduled for shipment. What is suitable?
options: Ship because the date has arrived.
Remove its label and mix it with good items.
Keep it identified and separated, and ask quality staff.
Relax the criteria and pass it.
reasons: A shipping date does not establish an unjudged item as conforming.
Removing the label and mixing loses status and target identification, risking escape.
Prevent unconfirmed items leaving and obtain an authorized judgment.
There is no authority to relax the criteria, and doing so does not resolve the unjudged state.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-10-q01.stem: Before approaching someone who may be receiving an electric shock, what is suitable?
options: Pull their hand to rescue them immediately.
Assume any nearby piece of wood is safe.
Touch to check whether electricity is present.
Do not touch directly; report and carry out possible stopping from a safe position.
reasons: Direct hand contact may expose the rescuer to shock.
A nearby wooden object may not meet the necessary conditions; do not approach an unknown energized state.
Checking electricity with the body itself creates shock danger.
Avoid secondary harm to the rescuer; do not contact an unknown energized state.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-10-q02.stem: A circuit breaker repeatedly trips. What should happen before restart?
options: Keep resetting and running.
Report the conditions and obtain the responsible person’s cause and safety checks.
Disable protection.
Replace it with a higher rating without authorization.
reasons: Repeated resets without cause confirmation can re-energize an abnormal condition.
Do not keep resetting while the cause of protective operation remains unknown.
Disabling protection removes the ability to interrupt dangerous faults.
Replacement without checking required ratings or equipment conditions can defeat suitable protection.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-10-q03.stem: Can any plastic sheet serve as protection for energized work?
options: No; check material conditions and its specification as protective equipment.
Yes; the material name guarantees safety.
Dirt and damage are irrelevant.
Performance is unlimited at high temperature.
reasons: Insulation performance depends on voltage, temperature, damage and related conditions.
The material name alone does not guarantee protection at the required voltage or condition.
Dirt and damage may affect insulation, so condition checks are necessary.
Temperature limits apply; performance is not necessarily maintained without limits in heat.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-10-q04.stem: A device has stopped, so someone says its capacitor terminals may be touched with a tool. What should you do?
options: A stopped indication alone proves discharge.
Short the terminals to check.
Do not touch; have residual energy checked by designated personnel and procedures.
If it looks similar, treat it like a battery.
reasons: A stopped display does not prove stored energy has disappeared.
Independently shorting terminals is not a safe discharge-verification procedure.
Energy can remain after power is off, and unauthorized shorting is dangerous.
A capacitor and battery have different mechanisms; check the item’s specifications and handling.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-10-q05.stem: You want to identify a part used for amplification or on/off control. Which explanation is suitable?
options: Check this as a transistor function.
A diode is only for amplification.
A capacitor always emits light.
Every similarly shaped part is identical.
reasons: Transistors are used for amplification or switching; match function and part number.
This confuses a diode’s one-direction conduction with transistor amplification and control.
A capacitor serves temporary storage and related functions; it is not necessarily a light-emitting part.
The same shape can conceal different functions, terminals or ratings.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-10-q06.stem: In equal-weight practice scoring, theory is 19/30 and practical 10/10. What do the app’s independent conditions give?
options: 29/40 in total guarantees a pass.
Perfect practical marks remove the need for theory.
Judge by combining theory and practical times.
Theory misses the required 20, so both sections have not passed.
reasons: Even a high combined total does not meet the separate theory minimum.
Practical marks do not replace taking theory and meeting its minimum.
Managing time and deciding each section’s pass result are different conditions.
Practice requires at least 20 theory and 6 practical answers correct independently.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-10-q07.stem: A study group proposes memorizing and sharing actual exam questions. How should you proceed?
options: A private group is always permitted.
Take out only part of the answers.
Use original general examples without collecting or recreating actual questions.
Share if the invigilator cannot see.
reasons: Avoid sharing actual questions or answers whether publicly or privately.
Even partial actual questions or answers must not be taken out or shared.
The source warns against taking out or sharing actual questions and answers.
Follow fair-exam and information rules, rather than basing conduct on visibility to an invigilator.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-10-q08.stem: A ground wire is connected. May isolation checks for internal inspection be omitted?
options: Grounding removes every shock hazard.
No; follow the equipment-specific isolation and related procedures.
Disassemble based only on the switch indication.
Leakage itself can no longer occur.
reasons: Grounding is part of protection, not removal of all shock danger.
Grounding does not replace the safety procedure for internal work.
A stopped indication alone does not meet isolation checks needed for internal work.
Grounding does not necessarily prevent leakage itself from occurring.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-10-q09.stem: Which matches equipment driving a pump with equipment changing voltage?
options: Both are circuit breakers only.
A motor only changes voltage.
A transformer necessarily produces hydraulic pressure.
A motor converts electricity to motion; a transformer changes voltage.
reasons: A breaker interrupts for protection; it does not replace both conversion functions.
A motor primarily converts electricity into mechanical power.
Transformer voltage conversion and hydraulic-pressure generation are different functions.
Distinguish motion, voltage conversion and protection.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-10-q10.stem: Which material uses electrical properties that vary with heat, light and related conditions?
options: Rubber of universally identical performance
Cross-section shape alone
A semiconductor
Packaging-paper color
reasons: Calling all rubber identical does not describe a semiconductor’s condition-dependent properties.
Cross-section alone does not explain classification by heat- or light-dependent electrical behavior.
Semiconductors use condition-dependent properties in electronic parts and related applications.
Packaging-paper color does not establish a material’s semiconductor function.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-10-q11.stem: An LED and another part share the same outline. What is needed before replacement?
options: Declare them interchangeable from outline alone.
Check drawing role, part number, terminals and ratings.
Try power; lighting is sufficient.
Reverse direction removes the need for rating checks.
reasons: An equal outline does not establish suitability for the drawing role, terminals or ratings.
Appearance alone does not establish compatible function, direction and ratings.
Trying power on an unknown part is not a safe method of selecting a suitable component.
Both direction and ratings require checking; reverse operation is not unconditionally permitted.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-10-q12.stem: You read only part of「してはいけない」and judged it as「してよい」. How should study improve?
options: Read through the ending, including conditions and negation, and check the situation and meaning.
Knowing technical terms makes endings unnecessary.
Fix unknown words’ meanings by guessing.
Never recheck after one reading.
reasons: Endings and conditions can reverse meaning, so read the whole statement.
Even known technical terms can be changed by sentence-ending negation or conditions.
Do not fix an unknown meaning by guessing; ask about the target and meaning.
Reading once does not guarantee understanding; recheck conditions and sentence endings.
